learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithmics; statistics and optimization.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.

Be able to identify their own training needs in their field of study and work or professional environment and to organize their own learning with a high degree of autonomy in all types of contexts (structured or not).

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.

That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Knowledge and understanding: Knowledge and understanding of mathematics and other basic sciences inherent to their engineering specialty, at a level that allows them to acquire the rest of the degree's competencies.
Knowledge and understanding: Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and apply relevant established analytical, computational, and experimental methods; and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems of their specialty, that meet established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as to select and apply appropriate project methods.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project, and research, and their limitations in their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology, and engineering processes and their limitations in their specialty.
Judgment making: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and cooperate with engineers as well as people from other disciplines.
Makes decisions and assesses the possible consequences of the selected alternative.
Uses descriptive statistics methods to describe data groups graphically and numerically. Generates simple and multiple linear regression models and uses them to make predictions.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, and making correct use of written language.
Knows and uses the main sampling distributions to calculate parameters and solve hypothesis testing problems.
Understands and uses the concept of probability. Knows the theorems of probabilistic spaces and uses them to analyze and predict the results of a random experiment.
Understands and uses the concept of random variable. Knows and uses the main discrete and continuous random variables.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, and making correct use of oral language.
Coordinates their work with other team members, contributes to their team in the development of tasks to be performed, and the creation of a good working environment.

teaching_methods: Development, writing, and presentation of reports, memos, audiovisual material, etc. related to projects/POPBLs, performed individually or in teams
Computer simulation practices, individually and/or in teams
Individual study and work, tests, exams and/or checkpoints
Completion of exercises individually and in teams
Classroom presentation in participatory classes, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work done, results obtained, documentation delivered, presentation, and technical defense
Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on the performance of exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices

assessment_rules: For projects, the final corrected memory version will serve as recovery. For the individual practice linked to RGM205, if not approved, another practice will be done, with the first weighing 25% and the second 75%. For individual tests linked to RGM206, the first test weighs 25%, and a second, if necessary, weighs 75%. For other individual written and oral tests, the same assessment method is used for recovery.
